title: Search bias, baselines and robustness

objectives.text: Explain why optimizing a noisy validation score selects noise, and evaluate a frozen choice against later held-out/baseline evidence under matched assumptions.
Compute a bounded exact one-sided fair-sign null p-value and fixed-family Bonferroni adjustment, stating marginal null validity, trial-family and dependence/market limits.

blocks.markdown: Searching thresholds, features, seeds, universes, dates, execution/cost assumptions and stopping times can fit noise even when the final model has few parameters. Reporting only the best score hides the search. Cawley/Talbot document that overfitting the selection criterion can materially bias evaluation. A validation score used to choose a candidate is a selection score, not independent performance evidence for the winner.

Own synthetic validation means: A 5, B 6, cash 0 bps. Choose B using validation only, with deterministic lexical tie rule. Later holdout means: A -2, B -4, cash 0. Report B validation 6 and later -4 alongside cash 0, not a silent switch to the holdout winner cash. This one example illustrates a possible selection failure; it does not estimate how often failures happen or prove every selected model loses. A valid strategy can also underperform over a short holdout.

blocks.title: One impressive trial versus a declared family

steps.text: Under an explicitly iid fair-sign null, eight independent +1 signs have one-sided tail probability 1/256. The statistic counts positive signs; it ignores economic magnitudes and costs.
If this is one of a fixed family of 20 valid marginal tests, Bonferroni adjusted p=min(1,20/256)=5/64≈0.078125. At predeclared alpha 0.05, the raw test rejects but the adjusted family test does not.

Union bound: if each true-null test has P(p_i<=alpha/m)<=alpha/m, then probability of any false rejection<=sum(alpha/m)<=alpha. Tests need not be independent from each other, but their marginal p-values and the declared finite family must be valid. This does not repair invalid time-series sign assumptions or hidden/adaptive trials.

blocks.caption: Expected 1/256 5/64 True False; B 6 -4; invalid fair-sign sample. Complete exact Fraction/binomial tail source, not estimated Monte Carlo p. Family size supplied by caller must match actual predefined comparisons;code cannot discover omitted trials, validate iid market signs or correct arbitrary adaptive experimentation. No t-test/Sharpe significance or real trading returns inferred.

blocks.markdown: A p-value is a null-tail probability for a specified statistic/protocol, not the probability the strategy is false or a guarantee a rejection will profit. The fair-sign model assumes independent signs, each equally likely positive/negative under the null, with no zeros here. Market returns may be dependent/asymmetric, net of costs and continuous magnitudes;converting them blindly to this toy p-value is unjustified. Failure to reject does not establish no effect, and significance does not establish economic relevance.

Compare against an appropriate no-trade/cash, passive or simple strategy baseline with matched universe, timing, exposure/currency, data, cost/financing and evaluation interval. A high gross return from leverage or omitted costs is not automatically excess skill. Predeclare economic metrics, drawdown/turnover/liquidity exposure and acceptable failure modes, then show tradeoff/sensitivity rather than only a winning Sharpe. Cash baseline return is 0 ONLY in this declared zero-interest synthetic example.

Perturb defensible assumptions within an a-priori grid: costs/delays, capacity, periods, universes and nearby parameter values. Report the whole surface and failure regions, including valid runs with poor outcomes. Repeated robustness exploration becomes more search; do not relabel only favorable perturbations as confirmation. Costs can alter path and lower fills can avoid losses, so empirical responses need interpretation rather than a universal monotonic slogan.

Nested evaluation fits/chooses the full procedure within each inner training/validation loop, and evaluates it on outer held-out data. sklearn's Iris example explains the selection principle but uses shuffled classification folds;do NOT copy that splitting into historical market forecasting. Use time/label-aware inner AND outer boundaries and train-only preprocessing from the prior lesson. Nested evaluation estimates the tested procedure under its data assumptions, not tomorrow's regime or a cure for every hidden human research choice.

Independent transfer: enumerate all 2^n sign sequences for small n and check the exact tail count/p-value superuniform property under the stated fair null. Compare raw and fixed-family adjustment at predeclared alpha, then explain why unrecorded/adaptive trials break the given accounting. Freeze a candidate before reading a separate holdout, compare a same-rules baseline, and publish failures as well as scores. No positive result is a professional/trading competence certificate.

Sources: [Cawley/Talbot 2010 original model-selection-bias paper page](http://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html), [sklearn nested selection principle, Iris not market folds](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/auto_examples/model_selection/plot_nested_cross_validation_iris.html), [NIST Bonferroni general inequality](https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/prc/section4/prc473.htm). Fair-sign exact tail and fixed-family p-adjustment are derived here from binomial counting/union bound, not a new market inference method.

summary: Selection searches can overfit validation noise; freeze choices and report later matched-baseline evidence honestly. Exact toy fair-sign/Bonferroni arithmetic needs valid null marginals and a declared family, not hidden adaptive trials. Robustness/nested time-aware evaluation remain scoped, not future-profit guarantees.
